L.B.Nagar, Hyderabad And ... on 11 September, 2024

The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1162 of 2010
Judgment:

This appeal is filed by the claimants aggrieved by the order dated 05.03.2010 in O.P.No.429 of 2008 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (Principal District Judge), Nalgonda (for short 'the Tribunal').

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (Principal District Judge), Nalgonda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel appearing for both sides and perused the record.
3.
The appellants are the dependants of the deceased.

On 15.01.2018, while the deceased was going on his motor cycle, when he reached outskirts of Mothkur Village, the offending vehicle, which is a Jeep bearing No. AP-23-C-3225, came in opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motor cycle, resulting in the deceased sustaining injuries and died on the spot.
4. The manner in which the accident has taken place and the liability on the Insurance Company are not disputed.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant would submit that the Tribunal has committed an error in considering the age of the mother of the deceased while concluding compensation.
Apparently, it is incorrect.
As per Ex.A2/post-mortem report, the KS,J age of the deceased was 26 years at the time of accident and the same has to be considered for concluding the compensation.
6. On perusal of the record, it appears that the deceased was bachelor and aged 26 years when the death happened.
Further, the deceased was working as a Police Constable and he was earning a sum of Rs.7,775/- per month as per Ex.A5/pay slip.

7. Relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 1, if 50% of his income is added towards future prospects, the monthly income would come to Rs.11,662/- (Rs.7,775/- + (50% of 7,775)).

Delhi Transport Corporation 2, and thus, the monthly contribution of the deceased to the claimants would be Rs.5,831/- (11,662- (1/2nd of 11,662)).

sentences.text: Then annual contribution comes to Rs.69,972/-.
As per Schedule II of the Act, if the said annual contribution arrived is multiplied with relevant multiplier i.e., '17' to the age of the deceased, the total amount comes to Rs.11,89,524/-.
The claimants are entitled for the said amount under the head of loss of dependency.
Further, relying on the ratio laid down in Pranay Sethi's case (2 supra), the claimants are granted Rs.30,000/- towards funeral expenses and loss of estate.
Further, each claimant is granted Rs.40,000/- towards consortium.

opennyai_summary.decision:
As there are two dependants (i.e., parents of the deceased) on the deceased, 1/2nd of his income is deducted towards personal expenditure as per the authority in Smt. Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation 2, and thus, the monthly contribution of the deceased to the claimants would be Rs.5,831/- (11,662- (1/2nd of 11,662)).
Then annual contribution comes to Rs.69,972/-.
As per Schedule II of the Act, if the said annual contribution arrived is multiplied with relevant multiplier i.e., '17' to the age of the deceased, the total amount comes to Rs.11,89,524/-.
The claimants are entitled for the said amount under the head of loss of dependency.
Further, relying on the ratio laid down in Pranay Sethi's case (2 supra), the claimants are granted Rs.30,000/- towards funeral expenses and loss of estate.
Further, each claimant is granted Rs.40,000/- towards consortium.
